newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Sept 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Analysts believe that resource stocks' current rally will only be temporary, with key metals like copper and aluminium leading a slump in commodity prices that will affect stocks into the next year. Page 1.

BHP Transport believes its new deal to use nine foreign-crewed ships to carry cargo between Australia and New Zealand has broken a two-decade-year-old Maritime Union "accord" restricting competition in trans-Tasman shipping. Page 3.

Australia has backed calls that the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation forum's goal of free and open trade by 2020 be accepted by the World Trade Organisation, but has criticised the low levels of business involvement in the forum saying more regional trade liberalisation is needed. Page 5.

Resolute Samantha Ltd yesterday announced that its A$184 million nickel plant at Bulong would begin production in 1998 and would generate A$3.5 billion over its 26-year minelife. The project, once online, will consider a A$300 million second stage that would treble production. Page 33.

James Hardie Industries Ltd will boost production of its highly popular US fibre cement siding board at two of its US plants. Current efficiency gains achieved with the current operations preceded this move. Page 33.

After announcing a net profit of A$229.9 million in its first year as a fully corporatised entity, AUSTA Electric, Queensland's largest power generating body, has called for greater competition in the State's electricity market. The call comes as the Government is about to receive a key report on the structure of the State's A$12.5 billion power industry. Page 35.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's two uranium oxide producers, Energy Resources of Australia Ltd and WMC Ltd, yesterday geared up for a multi-million-dollar export boom as the Federal Government announced the decision to revoke the eight-year ban on new sales contracts with France. Page 19.

The Reserve Bank of Australia yesterday hinted at further falls in home lending margins as Australian banks continued on the current cost squeeze by increasing fees and closing branches. Meanwhile the RBA disputed the Treasury argument to the Wallis inquiy that bank consumers should take on more of the risks associated with their own financial decisions. Page 19.

Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes yesterday slammed the Federal Government's decision to dump the research and development tax syndication scheme. Stokes was speaking at the opening of a A$100 million coal gasification plant in Victoria, claiming the plant in which he was a major backer, would never have been built under the new R & D rules. Page 19.

Tensions within the Australian National Industries Ltd board surfaced again yesterday as embattled directors Ross Palmer and Fred Smith rebuked the board for classifying their announcement which confirmed an investigation into ANI's deal to buy a German evironmental engineering company as "unauthorised". Page 21.

Australia's nickel mining boom received a further boost yesterday with Resolute Samantha Ltd announcing the go-ahead for its Bulong nickel and cobalt project in Western Australia. Resolute claims the mine will generate a cash flow of A$3.5 billion over it 26-year life, with production starting in the first half of 1998. Page 21.

The Federal Government has been urged to levy taxes on the family home by leading actuary KPMG. The politically unpalatable task of the taxation levy would be to ensure that personal savings were redirected into productive businesses. KPMG Actuaries head Bruce Edwards believes Australia's exports will not improve until we start directing investment into bigger factories "and not bigger lounge rooms." Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Investors seeking bank shares in the wake of the US Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates have pushed the National Australia Bank, Westpac Banking Corp and ANZ Banking Group shares to record highs despite the Reserve Bank warning that next year bank profitability will be slashed. Page 25.

The resource sector is not the only area of trading to be affected by the dumping of resources stocks, many of Australia's fund managers have been hurt as well in the sell-off. The hope that 1996 would be a strong year for world growth that would force up commodity prices and thus demand for mining shares, seems to have been premature. Page 25.

Ansett Australia's final hurdle before it forms an alliance with Air New Zealand, Air New Zealand's shareholder vote on whether to buy half of Ansett or not, has taken a hit from the Bureau of Air Safety Investigation releasing its final report into the cash-landing last year of one of Ansett's 747s. Page 25.

Qantas is desperately attempting to alter Air New Zealand's method of increasing the level of foreign ownership, including making representations to the New Zealand Stock Exchange. All measures so far seem to be ineffectual. Page 25.

According to a survey of 11 countries conducted yesterday, Australian business optimism about sales and profits has continued to increase for the third quarter in a row. These increases follow six consecutive quarters of declining optimism. Page 27.

The City of Melbourne councillors yesterday rejected a plan for the city to mount a joint bid for the Melbourne airport with Crown Casino developer Hudson Conway HDC.AX, but Lord Mayor Ivan Deveson convinced councillors to push forward with a bid. Page 27.
THE AGE

Transport Minister John Sharp is said to be trying to broker a deal with the ACTU, and the Maritime Union of Australia in order to sell the Australian National Shipping Line. BHP is expected to use one of the ships in its international fleet. Page C1.

Resolute Samantha has boosted Australia's growing nickel industry with its announcement that is will press ahead with plans at its Bulong project in Western Australia. The potential costs of these plans is around A$500 million. Page C1.

Many believe that like many other great inventions that have had great consumer durability, like the telephone, motor car and television, the Internet will be the next and may unite a generation into communicating, linking and trading via cyberspace as it gains popularity and becomes more and more affordable. Page C1.
Strength in Wall Street's transport index yesterday boosted shares in Brambles Industries over the A$20 mark for the first time. Bramble shares closed 50c stronger at a record A$20.20. Page C2.

The Reserve Bank believes that banks profits will be slashed next year by more than A$400 million due to intense competition from mortgage originators. The Reserve Bank's deputy governor Graeme Thompson said that the four big banks would have their equityreturns reduced by about one percentage point. Page C3.

Sources have stated that Vienna International Airport will supply Hudson Conway with airport operating services if it wins in its bid for the Melbourne Airport - an important link with the Federal Government nominating airport operating expertise as a keyfactor in any bid. Page C3
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
